schemaContract.policy: New BenchToActiveTriggerPolicy implements AbilityEventPolicy. Exact five JSON keys trigger/watch/turn/optional/usage; trigger ON_BENCH_TO_ACTIVE, watch SELF, turn OWN, boolean true optional, usage ONCE_PER_TURN only. Strings/boolean must have correct JSON types. No shared usage, alternate watch/turn, additional unknown keys or card-trigger source.
schemaContract.program: For this new policy only: exactly one matching trigger, no root/child conditions, exactly one move_energy node with precisely the approved arguments. Reject bind/all/distribution/card_kind/other filters/children/costs and arbitrary automatic programs. Keep all older policy validation unchanged.
schemaContract.moveExtension: AttachedEnergyEffect.destinationSelf remains backwards compatible for TRIGGER_POKEMON -> OWN_FIELD/SELF. Add a distinct exact helper otherOwnMetalToSelf for only ALL_OWN_POKEMON, amount120, minimum1, destination_scope OWN_FIELD, destination_ref SELF, energy_type METAL, count_mode CARDS with precisely these arguments and no conditions/children. Parse this reviewed shape before the unchanged generic amount<=60 branch. Any variation, including amount61 or121, rejects. This form requires a real captured incoming source context; manual Trainer/Attack/rule programs cannot invent it.
schemaContract.units: CARDS counts selected physical entities, not supplied units. Eligibility means currentEnergyProfile at the donor provides at least one METAL. One eligible multi-unit or all-type card moves whole. Any chosen subset of1..available is permitted, with an exact-new-form120 capacity covering both60-card decks. Candidate pools above120 reject as invalid match state rather than truncate. Card ownership is independent of field control; an opposing-owned attachment on an own donor remains eligible and retains its owner.
schemaContract.loader: No new ModInfo capability flag or UI/network transport. Existing BundledCombatData wraps policy effects into matching trigger after AbilityEventPolicy parsing. Existing EffectSchemaValidator delegates AttachedEnergyEffect parsing. EffectCardSelectionSpec, existing generic card selectors and ordinary AttachedEnergyEffect count bounds stay unchanged.
schemaContract.sourceDefinition: No card ID or Ability ID hardcoding in the engine. Strict event/effect shape provides the reviewed capability; converter separately matches exact actual text/identities.
schemaContract.selectionCapacity: EffectCardSelectionSpec remains unchanged at60: this attached-energy path never uses it. Add only EffectSelectionTransaction.openForOtherOwnMetalEnergy(owner,revision,exactDefinition,candidates), which checks AttachedEnergyEffect.otherOwnMetalToSelf, PUBLIC_FIELD PokemonTarget candidates owned/controlled by the entitled seat, distinct IDs and1..120 candidates, then uses a private120-capacity construction path. Existing public open/openForTarget retain60. The new factory is a server-side selection-shape validator, not authority to execute an Ability; the private captured transition token remains mandatory in ServerMatch preflight.

Reuse abilitySource and bindSourceEvent with triggerPokemon=sourcePokemon=the incoming logical entry. Reject unsupported trigger timing. capturedEventAndIdentity.preflight: ServerEffectExecutionContext for ON_BENCH_TO_ACTIVE requires automatic=true, a matching private captured transition token and captured source/event identity. Generic executeEffectProgramByRule with a real source UUID is still unauthorized. Token follows the existing nested context copy path if needed; exact96 program has no nested steps.
capturedEventAndIdentity.position: At resolution the destination is context.liveSourcePokemon, never current Active. Bench return preserves that field entry. The new ALL_OWN source form excludes this exact destination even when it is now Bench.
capturedEventAndIdentity.departure: A removed/re-entered logical entry cannot receive the old event’s Energy. If no live original destination remains, discard event without offering or reserving usage. No last-known off-field Energy destination.
capturedEventAndIdentity.definitionAndSuppression: Capture uses enabled Ability at movement. Subsequent handling follows existing captured field-event semantics: same logical field entry/program token persists; do not introduce a speculative global re-scan of all Abilities or a new switch reset. Source profile transformation and suppression after capture are inference boundaries to audit independently, not new card-specific rulings.
capturedEventAndIdentity.usage: Use existing abilitySource key (logical ID + ability ID + entry) and EffectLifecycleDispatcher ONCE_PER_TURN reservation. Capture/order/decline do not reserve. potentialAndSelection.captureTime: Bypass early EffectPotential.canAffect only for this policy, alongside existing narrowly named Checkup/95 exemptions. An empty donor pool at movement may become nonempty during the original text. Capture conditions are otherwise exact/no arbitrary root conditions.
potentialAndSelection.offerTime: At resolveOrOfferTriggeredAbility, before optional prompt and again before accepting use, verify transition turn is still current, original source entry exists, no pending confirmed/HP KO for it, usage remains available, and the current exact program can change state via a qualifying other-own donor. Failure silently drops that captured opportunity without consuming usage. It does not create a late manual action. Other simultaneous events may change this potential before the chosen event is considered.
potentialAndSelection.minimum: If offered, optional decline consumes no usage. Recheck late potential immediately before beginCaptured reserves usage. Accept opens the exact public attached-energy transaction with minimum1; never reconstruct the exact contract with minimum0. Empty selection is rejected atomically; repeated/stale/wrong-owner commands preserve cursor, selection and RNG. If source/potential is stale at acceptance, drop the captured opportunity without reserving usage. The one-node program has no intervening state-changing prefix; an unexpected zero pool at opening is an invariant error, never a min0 downgrade.
potentialAndSelection.sourceCandidates: New helper filters ALL_OWN_POKEMON through captured live destination and excludes identical host before enumerating attachments. Potential and actual selection share the exact donor/type/destination predicate, including a pure check that the donor permits this Ability effect (never call replay-mutating preventCardEffect during a query). A protected destination can still produce the existing detach-to-owner-discard change. Include a later new Active donor when source returned to Bench. Exclude opponent hosts and source own attachments; do not exclude an eligible card solely because its physical owner differs from its host controller. Pure protection predicate is ServerMatch.preventsImpact(owner,pokemon,capturedOrigin,OTHER_EFFECTS), baseline469; use context origin rather than chooser or ambient current actor.
potentialAndSelection.commit: Before any move, revalidate ALL selected physical IDs, donor logical entry and attachment identity, current effective METAL eligibility, and destination captured entry. New form compares resolved selections with freshly computed candidates, closing the existing generic MOVE path type-recheck gap only for this capability. Validate selected size<=120 and all IDs before movement; a121 request fails atomically even if synthetic data supplies it. No prefix movement before all selected identities pass.
potentialAndSelection.destination: Existing destination_ref SELF auto-commits the unique fixed destination; no player-selected second host. Keep original Ability origin for protection. Donor protection/no-effect and destination rejection/discard semantics follow existing reviewed move implementation; do not route through hand attachment quota/lock.
potentialAndSelection.atomicityAndKO: Validate whole selection before grouping moves. Keep resolvingEffectProgram active across every donor group; settle HP and invalid host attachments after the full transfer step/Ability checkpoint. Losing a donor HP modifier or gaining a receiver modifier may cause KOs only at that whole-step boundary, never while toggling choices or after the first selected card.
potentialAndSelection.energyEvents: Preserve existing moveAttachedEnergyByEffect semantics for attachment events, ownership, restrictions and cleanup. Do not fabricate a from-hand attach, hand-play history or manual Energy quota. Transferred card’s actual owner remains unchanged.
potentialAndSelection.actualSupplyCases: Actual me4_en_085 Magnet Metal is supported. Actual Reversal sv2_en_192 can provide three all-type units on qualifying evolved non-rulebox donor while behind on prizes, then one Colorless on Basic ex destination. Neo Upper sv5_en_162 remains unsupported and may only be an explicitly synthetic equivalent in tests.
potentialAndSelection.capacityAtOpen: openPendingAttachedEnergy takes an explicit exact-form branch: preserve the original constant amount120/minimum1 definition, compute all current candidates, reject more than120, and openForOtherOwnMetalEnergy with transaction maximum=candidate count (1..120). Do not fall back through generic open or the existing Math.min(minimum,available) contract rewrite. Subsequent commit reparses the same exact definition, so it cannot lose the120 capability.
potentialAndSelection.productLabel: Add an exact-form branch in ServerMatch.attachedEnergyLabel: describe choosing Energy cards providing Metal from other own Pokemon and moving them to this Ability source, with at least1. Do not present120 as a printed card cap or say the user chooses another destination. Existing generic labels remain unchanged; the generic prompt min/max still reports the actual candidate bound.

continuationAndOrdering.fullOriginalText: Capture never drains in the producer. Original attack/Trainer/Ability completes all suffix choices, draw and attachments before the incoming opportunity is offered, as Surfer analogue explicitly rules. Existing resolvingEffectProgram/advancingResolution/pendingResolution guards handle this.
continuationAndOrdering.oldEvents: Do not replace or rename ON_RETREAT/ON_SWITCH. Suggested minimal private change: capturePokemonChangeEvent returns its allocated batch ID (existing statement callers can ignore it), and incoming capture appends to that same batch for the same successful swap. This preserves existing ordering when96 absent and lets existing current-player trigger ordering choose among coexisting outgoing/incoming events rather than imposing invented precedence. KO promotion uses a fresh event batch; sequential required promotions remain distinct.
continuationAndOrdering.damageAndKO: Do not add96 to95 pre-KO priority or bypass attack/ON_KNOCKOUT gates. Finish original text, existing damage reactions and required KO processing; only surviving live source receives the incoming optional use. This is deliberately different from the off-field95 capture.
continuationAndOrdering.promotionHP: Keep resumeAfterKnockouts currentHitPointKnockouts check before any new optional offer. Bench-only maxHP lost by promotion can produce immediate cascading KO; resolve it and existing prizes/replacements first. A queued incoming event for the removed entry becomes ineligible. The optional Energy transfer cannot rescue an already-depleted/confirmed KO source. This follows manual I D p12 general timing, not a direct Metal Road FAQ.
continuationAndOrdering.ownAttack: Normal completed attack already uses continueCurrentTurn=true plus endingResumableAttack: after promotion, drain captured incoming event while it is still owner turn, then finishResumableAttackTurn advances exactly once. Keep queued/in-flight/optional and Energy selection pauses blocking turn progression.
continuationAndOrdering.ownTurnEnd: turnEndInProgress true survives end-turn direct KO and promotion. Resume TURN_END, process incoming optional event and any legal transfer, then continue remaining end-turn queue/checkup exactly once. Do not restart runTurnEnd or duplicate expiry.
continuationAndOrdering.legacyFalseBranch: Failed Confusion KO at baseline7703 calls resolveKnockouts(...false); the default resumeAfterKnockouts branch would otherwise end the turn before96. In resumeAfterKnockouts, restore phase, then BEFORE currentHitPointKnockouts, ToolOverflow return or the first drain: if !resolvingCheckup && !turnEndInProgress && !resumeCurrentTurnAfterReplacement and a private captured incoming96 opportunity is queued/in-flight, set endingPromotionTurn=true. This is a one-shot continuation obligation for the current player turn, not another Ability event. Do not clear or recompute it when its source dies, the queue drains/drops, or a later KO sets resumeCurrentTurnAfterReplacement=true.
continuationAndOrdering.cleanup: finish/concede clears endingPromotionTurn and incoming queued/pending state through existing cleanup. Rejected selections or stale requests do not clear it. The flag is latched before HP cascading can overwrite continueCurrentTurn and persists until the one completion gate; it is not derived from queue non-emptiness after first capture. Never set it for a normal manual switch/retreat, already-ending TURN_END, Checkup, or a continuation that originally means the current turn may continue.
continuationAndOrdering.sameActionBatchStatus: Batch-sharing proposal is an implementation ordering contract using existing current-player event dispatcher, not a separately obtained Metal Road-vs-outgoing-retreat FAQ. Independent audit should review before approval.
continuationAndOrdering.falseBranchResume: After the existing HP check (which remains before any optional offer), branch on resumeCurrentTurnAfterReplacement OR endingPromotionTurn: clear only resumeCurrentTurnAfterReplacement, restore player/end-turn phase as appropriate, and drain. If endingPromotionTurn is true and ToolOverflow is pending, return before optional processing and retain it. The ordinary checkup/false/no96 path remains unchanged. All later KO checkpoints may still write their existing continueCurrentTurn value; the independent endingPromotionTurn survives them.
continuationAndOrdering.completionGate: Extend finishResumableAttackTurn to regard endingPromotionTurn as an ending obligation alongside the existing attack/card flags. Retain all current guards: phaseTURN, no ToolOverflow, no original/automatic program in flight, no pendingResolution, no attack/KO checkpoint, no ordering/optional prompt, no queued reactions and no95 checkpoint. Only this gate clears all ending flags together BEFORE calling runTurnEnd once. Repeated outer finally/submit/discardOverflowTool calls then see no obligation. finish/concede clears it without entering turn end.
continuationAndOrdering.toolOverflow: discardOverflowTool already resumes settleHitPointChanges, saved tool effect checkpoints, pendingResolution/drain and finishResumableAttackTurn. Keep those routes and deferred direct-KO sets intact. A correction-triggered HP KO uses resolveEffectKnockouts(...continueCurrentTurn=true); this must not overwrite endingPromotionTurn. If more tools remain, preserve it through the early return. After final correction, a surviving queued event can offer; a removed/no-potential event drops; either route ends once after prizes/replacements and remaining effects. toolTurnAdvancePending is the separate already-started Checkup/expiry continuation and must not be repurposed to store this obligation.
falseBranchStateCases: False-continue Confusion KO ->96 promotion ->optional accept/pause/transfer ->one turn-end/Checkup/draw.
Same transition ->decline OR no current eligible donor ->queue empty ->same one-shot ending gate.
Promoted source loses Bench-only HP ->second KO before offer ->prizes/replacement ->old source token drops; any surviving new incoming opportunity is handled, then exactly one ending gate.
Promotion/transfer causes ToolOverflow ->pause ->several corrections; final correction causes HP KO with continueCurrentTurn=true ->marker survives prizes/replacement ->one ending gate.
Concede or terminal prize/no-Pokemon result at any pause ->finish clears marker; no turn-end/Checkup/next draw.
All no96 legacy branches and normal manual96 use preserve their prior turn continuation behavior.
